 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::allocate_pattern
 (   ) 

This method allocates a pattern containing svt_pattern_data instances for all of the primitive data fields in the object. The name is set to the corresponding field name, the value is set to 0.

Return values - An svt_pattern instance containing entries for all of the data fields.

  function bit
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::decode_prop_val
 (  string prop_name , bit [1023:0] prop_val , ref string prop_val_string , input svt_pattern_data :: type_enum typ  ) 

Simple utility used to convert 'bit [1023:0]' property value representation into its equivalent string property value representation. Extended to support decoding of enum values.

prop_name - The name of the property being encoded.

prop_val_string - The string describing the value to be encoded.

prop_val - The bit vector encoding of prop_val_string.

typ - Optional field type used to help in the encode effort.

Return values - The enum value corresponding to the desc.

  function bit
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::get_prop_val
 (  string prop_name , ref bit [1023:0] prop_val , input int array_ix , ref svt_sequence_item_base data_obj  ) 

This method is used by a component's command interface, to allow command code to retrieve the value of a single named property of a data class derived from this class. If the prop_name argument does not match a property of the class, or if the array_ix argument is not zero and does not point to a valid array element, this function returns '0'. Otherwise it returns '1', with the value of the prop_val argument assigned to the value of the specified property. However, If the property is a sub-object, a reference to it is assigned to the data_obj (ref) argument.

prop_name - The name of a property in this class, or a derived class.

prop_val - A ref argument used to return the current value of the property, expressed as a 1024 bit quantity. When returning a string value each character requires 8 bits so returned strings must be 128 characters or less.

array_ix - If the property is an array, this argument specifies the index being accessed. If the property is not an array, it should be set to 0.

data_obj - If the property is not a sub-object, this argument is assigned to null. If the property is a sub-object, a reference to it is assigned to this (ref) argument. In that case, the prop_val argument is meaningless. The component will then store the data object reference in its temporary data object array, and return a handle to its location as the prop_val argument of the get_data_prop task of the component. The command testbench code must then use that handle to access the properties of the sub-object.

Return values - A single bit representing whether or not a valid property was retrieved.

 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::set_prop_val
 (  string prop_name , bit [1023:0] prop_val , int array_ix  ) 

This method is used by a component's command interface, to allow command code to set the value of a single named property of a data class derived from this class. This method cannot be used to set the value of a sub-object, since sub-object construction is taken care of automatically by the command interface. If the prop_name argument does not match a property of the class, or it matches a sub-object of the class, or if the array_ix argument is not zero and does not point to a valid array element, this function returns '0'. Otherwise it returns '1'.

prop_name - The name of a property in this class, or a derived class.

prop_val - The value to assign to the property, expressed as a 1024 bit quantity. When assigning a string value each character requires 8 bits so assigned strings must be 128 characters or less.

array_ix - If the property is an array, this argument specifies the index being accessed. If the property is not an array, it should be set to 0.

Return values - A single bit representing whether or not a valid property was set.

 rand bit  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::force_enable_line_sampling = 0

This variable is to indicate that RX FSM should be enabled in case it was disabled by the CPHY lane module or upper layer internally.
  • If respective C-PHY lane module only support unidirectional flow from MASTER -> SLAVE, then TX FSM is enabled and RX FSM is disabled in active unidirectional MASTER CPHY lane modules.
  • Transmitted data is not sampled from the interface lines(A,B & C) for active unidirectional MASTER CPHY lane modules. Transmitted lane transaction is directly send to the respective analysis port/upper layer once TX FSM transmission is over.
  • To enable these line based sampling for active unidirectional MASTER CPHY lane modules, set this variable value to one.
  • SLAVE CPHY lane module RX FSM is enable by default irrespective the value of this variable.
  • For bi-directional CPHY MASTER/SLAVE lane module RX FSM is by default enabled with TX FSM.
  • This variable has no relevance in case of bi-directional CPHY lane module/SLAVE CPHY lane module. Implicitly upper layer take cares to enable the RX FSM.
  • Default is 0.

 rand bit [3:0]   attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::lpdt_bit_pause[]

This array stores the bit positions within an LPDT byte boundary 'after' which LPDT bit pause will be introduced.

  • Even values correspond to LPDT data bits i.e. if any array element value is 0, it signifies that bit pause will be introduced after first data bit is transmitted.

  • Odd values corresponds to space states i.e. if any array element value is 1, it signifies that bit pause will be introduced after first space state is transmitted.

  • Valid values are 0 to 15 (represents 8 data bits and 8 space states).

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::lpdt_bit_pause_duration_max = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_LPDT_BIT_PAUSE_DURATION_MAX

This variable is used to specify the maximum pause delay in between two consecutive bits within a LPDT transaction. The VIP randomly generates a delay value based on the specified lpdt_bit_pause_duration_min and lpdt_bit_pause_duration_max range.

  • This delay value will be considered as maximum range value for generating the pause duration after the transmission of the specified bit within a byte boundary.

  • This delay value specifies the maximum number of ESC clk pulse(s) for which the VIP may remain in pause duration.

  • Default is SVT_MIPI_CPHY_LPDT_BIT_PAUSE_DURATION_MAX (5).

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::lpdt_bit_pause_duration_min = 1

This variable is used to specify the minimum pause delay value in between two consecutive bits within a LPDT transaction. The VIP randomly generates a delay value based on the specified lpdt_bit_pause_duration_min and lpdt_bit_pause_duration_max range.

  • This delay value will be considered as minimum range value for generating the pause duration after the transmission of the specified bit within a byte boundary.

  • This delay value specifies the minimum number of ESC clk pulse(s) for which the VIP may remain in pause duration.

  • Default is 1

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::lpdt_byte_pause_duration_max = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_LPDT_BYTE_PAUSE_DURATION_MAX

This variable is used to specify the maximum pause delay value in between two consecutive LPDT byte transactions. The VIP randomly generates a delay value based on the specified lpdt_byte_pause_duration_min and lpdt_byte_pause_duration_max range.

  • This delay value will be considered as maximum range value for the pause duration prior to the transmission of LPDT byte transaction.

  • This delay value specifies the maximum number of ESC clk pulse(s) for which the VIP may remain in pause duration.

  • Default is SVT_MIPI_CPHY_LPDT_BYTE_PAUSE_DURATION_MAX (25)

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::lpdt_byte_pause_duration_min = 1

This variable is used to specify the minimum pause delay value in between two consecutive LPDT byte transactions. The VIP randomly generates a delay value based on the specified lpdt_byte_pause_duration_min and lpdt_byte_pause_duration_max range.

  • This delay value will be considered as minimum range value for generating the pause duration prior to the transmission of LPDT byte transaction.

  • This delay value specifies the minimum number of ESC clk pulse(s) for which the VIP may remain in pause duration.

  • Default is 1

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::lpdt_byte_pause_xactions[]

This array stores the transactions for which LPDT pause feature will be enabled.

  • If lpdt_bit_pause_array size is non-zero, LPDT bit pause will be introduced for respective transaction numbers stored in lpdt_byte_pause_xactions array.

  • If lpdt_pause_on_byte_boundary = 1, byte pause will be introduced before the respective transaction number stored in lpdt_byte_pause_xactions array.

  • If lpdt_pause_on_byte_boundary = 0, no byte pause will be introduced.

This variable is used to enable LPDT pause functionality at byte boundary.

  • 1 : Enabled
  • Default is 0 (Disabled)

 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_eot_all_ones = 1'b1

Indicates whether first eot word will be all ones or all zeros.

 rand bit  attribute

Indicates EOT APP processing.
  • This configuration is applicable only to PPI_PHY_REMOTE and PPI_PHY_SERIAL mode.
  • Set to 1'b1 if eot processing is done at the APP which means one or more EOT words are appended at the end of the data transmission.
  • Set to 1'b0 if eot processing is done at the PHY level.
  • Default value is 1'b0.

 rand bit  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_force_rx_user_mode = 1'b0

This configuration is used to override the force_rx_mode setting done by the APP layer. When set, the ppi_force_rx_user_value is used in place of force_rx_mode set by APP. In PPI_APP_LOCAL mode, when this configuration is set then ppi_force_rx_user_value is assigned to the force_rx_mode at the PPI interface else the force_rx_mode set by APP is assigned.
  • Default value is 1'b0.
NOTE: It is recommended to set the user mode at initialization or at stop state when no transaction communication is happening on the lines.

When ppi_force_rx_user_mode is set, the ppi_force_rx_user_value is used in place of force_rx_mode set by APP. In PPI_APP_LOCAL mode, this value is assigned to force_rx_mode at PPI interface when ppi_force_rx_user_mode is set else the force_rx_mode set by APP is assigned.
  • Default value is 1'b0.
NOTE: It is recommended to set the user mode at initialization or at stop state when no transaction communication is happening on the lines.

This is applicable only in remote topology while responding to ULPS transaction on TX lines or driving ULPS transaction on RX lines. This variable holds the maximum ULPS request duration for ULPS transaction which translates
  • To delay (in ns) between detection of ULPS request on TX lines and assertion of UlpsActiveNot signal at PPI interface while responding to ULPS request on TX lines i.e. in PPI_LOCAL_REMOTE_MODE topology.
  • To delay (in ns) between de-assertion of StopState signal and assertion of RxUlpsEsc/UlpsActiveNot signal at PPI interface when a ULPS transaction is received from the APP layer to be transmitted on the RX lines i.e. in PPI_REMOTE_LOCAL_MODE topology.

 rand bit [SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_RX_DATA_WIDTH_HS_VECTOR_WIDTH-1:0]  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_rx_data_width_hs = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_RX_WORD_VALID_HS_VECTOR_WIDTH

rx_data_width_hs to define the data width in hs mode for ppi rx signals and values are as follows:
  • Bit[1:0] = 2'b00, not used and reserved
  • Bit[1:0] = 2'b01, for 16-bit data width
  • Bit[1:0] = 2'b10, for 32-bit data width
  • Bit[1:0] = 2'b11, not used and reserved
  • The default value of this field is same as the user define SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_RX_WORD_VALID_HS_VECTOR_WIDTH which is 1 for 16 bits and 2 for 32 bits.

RX symbol clock period configuration required for generating rx_word_clk_hs in remote topology.
  • This configuration is applicable only for PPI_PHY_REMOTE topology

 rand bit  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_turn_disable_user_mode = 1'b0

This configuration is used to override the turn_disable setting done by the APP layer. When set, the ppi_turn_disable_user_value is used in place of turn_disable set by APP. In PPI_APP_LOCAL mode, when this configuration is set then ppi_turn_disable_user_value is assigned to the turn_disable at the PPI interface else the turn_disable set by APP is assigned.
  • Default value is 1'b0.
NOTE: It is recommended to set the user mode at initialization or at stop state when no transaction communication is happening on the lines.

 rand bit  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_turn_disable_user_value = 1'b0

This configuration is used to set the override value for turn_disable when in user override mode. When ppi_turn_disable_user_mode is set, the ppi_turn_disable_user_value is used in place of turn_disable set by APP. In PPI_APP_LOCAL mode, this value is assigned to turn_disable at PPI interface when ppi_turn_disable_user_mode is set else the turn_disable set by APP is assigned.
  • Default value is 1'b0.
NOTE: It is recommended to set the user mode at initialization or at stop state when no transaction communication is happening on the lines.

 rand svt_mipi_cphy_configuration :: ppi_turn_request_mode_enum  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_turn_request_signal_mode = PPI_TURN_REQUEST_RANDOM

Indicates PPI Turn Request signal Mode during trigger transactions. There are 3 variations.
  • PPI_TURN_REQUEST_PULSE: TurnRequest signal gets de-asserted after one (LP) clock.
  • PPI_TURN_REQUEST_UNTIL_BTA: TurnRequest signal gets de-asserted when direction flips/timeout happens.
  • PPI_TURN_REQUEST_RANDOM: TurnRequest signal gets de-asserted after random number of (LP) clocks. The random delay is generated between ppi_turn_request_assertion_min and ppi_turn_request_assertion_max variables and if the random delay overshoots the BTA completion (direction flip or timeout), it gets trimmed at BTA completion.
  • Default value is PPI_TURN_REQUEST_RANDOM.

  • Bit[1:0] = 2'b01, for 16-bit data width
  • Bit[1:0] = 2'b10, for 32-bit data width

  • The default value of this field is same as the user define SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TX_WORD_VALID_HS_VECTOR_WIDTH which is 1 for 16 bits and 2 for 32 bits.

 rand svt_mipi_cphy_configuration :: ppi_tx_lpdt_esc_mode_enum  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_lpdt_esc_signal_mode = PPI_TX_LPDT_ESC_RANDOM

Indicates PPI TxLpdtEsc signal Mode. There are 3 variations.
  • PPI_TX_LPDT_ESC_PULSE: TxLpdtEsc signal gets asserted when TxRequestEsc is asserted and gets de-asserted after one clk.
  • PPI_TX_LPDT_ESC_SAME_AS_REQ: TxLpdtEsc signal gets asserted when TxRequestEsc is asserted and gets de-asserted when TxRequestEsc gets de-asserted
  • PPI_TX_LPDT_ESC_RANDOM: TxLpdtEsc signal gets asserted when TxRequestEsc is asserted and gets de-asserted after random number of clks between the min/max range defined by ppi_tx_lpdt_esc_assertion_min and ppi_tx_lpdt_esc_assertion_max variables.
  • Default value is PPI_TX_LPDT_ESC_RANDOM.

 rand bit  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_lpdt_req_to_data_delay = 1'b0

This variable is used to indicate if there needs to be a delay (of one clock) between tx_request_esc and tx_data_esc. The byte boundary delay for the first data transaction if configured would start after this delay.
  • 0 : There is no delay.
  • 1 : There is one clock delay
  • The default value is 1'b0.

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_trigger_esc_assertion_max = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_ASSERTION_MAX

This variable is used to store the maximum assertion duration of the TxTriggerEsc signal at the PPI interface when PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_RANDOM mode is used.

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_trigger_esc_assertion_min = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_ASSERTION_MIN

This variable is used to store the minimum assertion duration of the TxTriggerEsc signal at the PPI interface when PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_RANDOM mode is used.

 rand svt_mipi_cphy_configuration :: ppi_tx_trigger_esc_mode_enum  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_trigger_esc_signal_mode = PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_RANDOM

Indicates PPI TxTriggerEsc signal Mode. There are 3 variations.
  • PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_PULSE: TxTriggerEsc signal gets asserted when TxRequestEsc is asserted and gets de-asserted after one clk.
  • PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_SAME_AS_REQ: TxTriggerEsc signal gets asserted when TxRequestEsc is asserted and gets de-asserted when TxRequestEsc gets de-asserted
  • PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_RANDOM: TxTriggerEsc signal gets asserted when TxRequestEsc is asserted and gets de-asserted after random number of clks between the min/max range defined by ppi_tx_trigger_esc_assertion_min and ppi_tx_trigger_esc_assertion_max variables. In case the random delay overshoots TxRequestEsc then TxTriggerEsc is de-asserted along with TxRequestEsc.
  • Default value is PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_RANDOM.

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_trigger_req_assertion_max = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TX_TRIGGER_REQ_ASSERTION_MAX

This variable is used to store the maximum assertion duration of the TxRequestEsc signal at the PPI interface during trigger transaction when PPI_TX_TRIGGER_REQ_RANDOM mode is used.

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_trigger_req_assertion_min = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TX_TRIGGER_REQ_ASSERTION_MIN

This variable is used to store the minimum assertion duration of the TxRequestEsc signal at the PPI interface during trigger transaction when PPI_TX_TRIGGER_REQ_RANDOM mode is used.

 rand svt_mipi_cphy_configuration :: ppi_tx_trigger_req_mode_enum  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_trigger_req_signal_mode = PPI_TX_TRIGGER_REQ_CALC

Indicates PPI TxRequestEsc signal Mode during trigger transactions. There are 3 variations.
  • PPI_TX_TRIGGER_REQ_CALC: TxRequestEsc signal gets asserted for the calculated duration of the approximate time the serial layer takes to unload the trigger transaction onto the serial line considering the dummy byte configuration.
  • PPI_TX_TRIGGER_REQ_RANDOM: TxRequestEsc signal gets asserted for a random number of clocks generated between ppi_tx_trigger_esc_assertion_min and ppi_tx_trigger_esc_assertion_max variables.
  • Default value is PPI_TX_TRIGGER_ESC_CALC.

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_ulps_esc_assertion_max = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TX_ULPS_ESC_ASSERTION_MAX

 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_ulps_esc_signal_mode = PPI_TX_ULPS_ESC_RANDOM

Indicates PPI TxUlpsEsc signal Mode. There are 3 variations.
  • PPI_TX_ULPS_ESC_PULSE: TxUlpsEsc signal gets asserted when TxRequestEsc is asserted and gets de-asserted after one clk.
  • PPI_TX_ULPS_ESC_SAME_AS_REQ: TxUlpsEsc signal gets asserted when TxRequestEsc is asserted and gets de-asserted when TxRequestEsc gets de-asserted
  • PPI_TX_ULPS_ESC_RANDOM: TxUlpsEsc signal gets asserted when TxRequestEsc is asserted and gets de-asserted after random number of clks between the min/max range defined by ppi_tx_ulps_esc_assertion_min and ppi_tx_ulps_esc_assertion_max variables. In case the random number of clocks overshoots the TxRequestEsc then TxUlpsEsc gets de-asserted along with TxRequestEsc
  • Default value is PPI_TX_ULPS_ESC_RANDOM.

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_ulps_exit_assertion_max = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TX_ULPS_EXIT_ASSERTION_MAX

This variable is used to store the maximum assertion duration of the TxUlpsExit signal at the PPI interface when PPI_TX_ULPS_EXIT_RANDOM mode is used.

 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_ulps_exit_assertion_min = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TX_ULPS_EXIT_ASSERTION_MIN

This variable is used to store the minimum assertion duration of the TxUlpsExit signal at the PPI interface when PPI_TX_ULPS_EXIT_RANDOM mode is used.

 rand svt_mipi_cphy_configuration :: ppi_tx_ulps_exit_mode_enum  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_tx_ulps_exit_signal_mode = PPI_TX_ULPS_EXIT_RANDOM

Indicates PPI TxUlpsExit signal Mode. There are 3 variations.
  • PPI_TX_ULPS_EXIT_PULSE: TxUlpsExit signal gets asserted when APP layer requests ULPS exit to PPI layer and gets de-asserted after one clk.
  • PPI_TX_ULPS_EXIT_SAME_AS_REQ: TxUlpsExit signal gets asserted when APP layer requests ULPS exit to PPI layer and gets de-asserted when TxRequestEsc gets de-asserted.
  • PPI_TX_ULPS_EXIT_RANDOM: TxUlpsExit signal gets asserted when APP layer requests ULPS exit to PPI layer and gets de-asserted after random number of clks between the min/max range defined by ppi_tx_ulps_exit_assertion_min and ppi_tx_ulps_exit_assertion_max variables. In case the random number of clocks overshoots the TxRequestEsc then TxUlpsExit gets de-asserted along with TxRequestEsc
  • Default value is PPI_TX_ULPS_EXIT_RANDOM.

 rand bit [2:0]   attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::preamble_check_en = 3'b100

Three bit vector values enable/disable protocol checks for Preamble phase (Prebegin, Progseq & Preend).
  • preamble_check_en[SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PREAMBLE_PREBEGIN_CHECK_EN_BIT] Enables/Disables Prebegin check (0=OFF, 1=ON)
  • preamble_check_en[SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PREAMBLE_PROGSEQ_CHECK_EN_BIT] Enables/Disables Progseq check (0=OFF, 1=ON)
  • preamble_check_en[SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PREAMBLE_PREEND_CHECK_EN_BIT] Enables/Disables Pre-end check (0=OFF, 1=ON).
  • Default value is 3'b100 (PREEND Check is enabled).

This variable is used to configure t-init timeout duration.

 rand bit [7:0]   attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::tgr_post_length = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_TGR_POST_LENGTH_MAX

tgr_post_length register bit mapping and default value is as follows:
  • Bit[7:5] Reserved, will be set to 0.
  • Bit[4:0] This field is used to set the number of symbols to be transmitted after sending programmable sequence.
  • The number of transmitted symbol is {(tgr_post_length[4:0] + 1) * 7}.
  • The default value of this field is 31 (0x1F).

 rand bit [7:0]   attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::tgr_preamble_length = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_TGR_PREBEGIN_LENGTH_MAX

tgr_preamble_length register bit mapping and default value is as follows:
  • Bit[7] This field is used to enable transmission of programmable sequence if set to 1. The default value of this field is 0.
  • Bit[6] Reserved, will be set to 0.
  • Bit[5:0] This field is used to set the number of symbols to be transmitted before sending programmable sequence.
  • The number of transmitted symbol is {(tgr_preamble_length[5:0] + 1) * 7}.
  • The default value of this field is 63 (0x3F).

  • Bit[7:6] Reserved, will be set to 0.
  • Bit[5:3] This field is used to set symbol1 sequence pattern to be transmitted while sending programmable sequence.
  • Bit[2:0] This field is used to set symbol0 sequence pattern to be transmitted while sending programmable sequence.
  • Valid range for Bit[5:3] and Bit[2:0] is 0 to 4, with 3 being the default value.

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::trigger_dummy_bytes_max = 0

This variable is used to define the maximum range of trigger dummy bytes.
  • Trigger_dummy_bytes_max value should be zero when dummy bytes transmission not required after trigger commands.
  • Trigger_dummy_bytes_max value should be non-zero and greater or equal to trigger_dummy_bytes_min, only in cases when dummy bytes transmission is required.
  • Model will randomly generate number of trigger dummy bytes value between trigger_dummy_bytes_min & trigger_dummy_bytes_max.
  • Generated value will indicate the number of trigger dummy bytes need to be transmitted.
  • Default is 0.

 rand int unsigned  attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::trigger_dummy_bytes_min = SVT_MIPI_CPHY_TRIGGER_DUMMY_BYTES_MIN

This variable is used to define the minimum range of trigger dummy bytes.
  • Trigger_dummy_bytes_min value should be zero when dummy bytes transmission not required after trigger commands.
  • Trigger_dummy_bytes_min value should be non-zero and smaller or equal to trigger_dummy_bytes_max, only in cases when dummy bytes transmission is required.
  • Model will randomly generate number of trigger dummy bytes value between trigger_dummy_bytes_min & trigger_dummy_bytes_max.
  • Generated value will indicate the number of trigger dummy bytes need to be transmitted.
  • Default is SVT_MIPI_CPHY_TRIGGER_DUMMY_BYTES_MIN (0)

 rand bit [1:0]   attribute
 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::trigger_dummy_bytes_value = 2

This variable is used to indicate dummy bytes value.
  • 0 : All zero value will be considered for dummy bytes.
  • 1 : All one value will be considered for dummy bytes.
  • 2 : Random value will be considered for dummy bytes.
  • 3 : Reserved(Not allowed).
  • Default is 2 (Random value)

 typedef interface  svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::CPHY_IF
General Description

This interface defines a CPHY interface used by the SVT CPHY Transactor to hold an instance of CPHY signal interface that can be used for communication with a DUT.

This interface has mutiple modports defined considering Transmitter or Receiver direction in HS/LP mode.

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about. Note that all other signals or registers within this interface can and should be ignored (they are VIP and/or interface internal control signals).

Required Interface Connections: The following CPHY interface signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

Signal Name Signal Description
Trios Interface Signals
A Corresponds to line A in a CPHY Lane
B Corresponds to line B in a CPHY Lane
C Corresponds to line C in a CPHY Lane
Clock Interface Signals
hs_tx_clk Transmitter high speed clock.
hs_rx_clk Recovered/testbench provided high speed clock.
lp_tx_clk Transmitter low power escape mode clock.
lp_rx_clk Receiver low power recovered escape mode clock.
Status Interface Signals
hs_xmtr_enable Indicates respective CPHY HS transmitter is Enabled/Disabled.
signal_direction Indicates current CPHY(Master/Slave) signal direction.

Debug Interface:

The following signals are available to help debug the CPHY modules

Signal Name Signal Description
Transmitter Side Debug Interface Signals
word_data Indicates transmitter’s present word data.
wire_state Indicates transmitter’s present wire state.
symbol Indicates transmitter’s present symbol value.
fsm_state Indicates transmitter’s present FSM state.
Receiver Side Debug Interface Signals
rcvr_word_data Indicates receiver’s present word data.
rcvr_wire_state Indicates receiver’s present wire state.
rcvr_symbol Indicates receiver’s present symbol value.
rcvr_fsm_state Indicates receiver’s present FSM state.

 typedef interface  svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::PPI_IF
General Description

This interface defines a CPHY PPI interface used by the SVT CPHY PPI Transactor to hold an instance of CPHY PPI interface that can be used for communication with a DUT.

This interface has multiple modports defined considering Transmitter or Receiver direction in HS/LP mode.

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about. Note that all other signals or registers within this interface can and should be ignored (they are VIP and/or interface internal control signals).

Required Interface Connections: The following CPHY PPI interface signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

Signal Name Signal Description
Clock Interface Signals
tx_symbol_clk_hs Transmitter high speed symbol clock.
tx_word_clk_hs Transmitter generated/testbench provided high speed word clock.
rx_word_clk_hs Receiver recovered/testbench provided high speed word clock.
tx_clk_esc Transmitter escape mode clock.
rx_clk_esc Receiver recovered/testbench generated escape mode clock.
High Speed Transmit Interface Signals
tx_request_hs Indicates transmit request for HS transmitter.
tx_data_width_hs Indicates data width 16 or 32 bit for HS transmitter.
tx_word_valid_hs Indicates word [1:0] validity for HS transmitter.
tx_data_hs Indicates data for HS transmitter.
tx_send_sync_hs Indicates sync word information for HS transmitter.
tx_ready_hs Indicates data acknowledgement for HS transmitter.
High Speed Receive Interface Signals
rx_active_hs Indicates active transaction for HS receiver.
rx_data_width_hs Indicates data width 16 or 32 bit for HS receiver.
rx_valid_hs Indicates word [1:0] validity for HS receiver.
rx_data_hs Indicates data for HS receiver.
rx_sync_hs Indicates sync word information for HS receiver.
rx_invalid_code_hs Indicates invalid code received for HS receiver.
Escape Mode Transmit Interface Signals
tx_request_esc Indicates escape request for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_lpdt_esc Indicates lpdt request for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_data_esc Indicates lpdt data for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_valid_esc Indicates lpdt data validity for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_ready_esc Indicates lpdt data acknowledgement for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_ulps_esc Indicates ulps request for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_ulps_exit Indicates ulps exit request for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_trigger_esc Indicates trigger request for Tx Escape Mode.
Escape Mode Receive Interface Signals
rx_lpdt_esc Indicates lpdt request for Rx Escape Mode.
rx_data_esc Indicates lpdt data for Rx Escape Mode.
rx_valid_esc Indicates lpdt data validity for Rx Escape Mode.
rx_ulps_esc Indicates ulps request for Rx Escape Mode.
rx_trigger_esc Indicates trigger request for Rx Escape Mode.
Control Interface Signals
enable Indicates to enable the PPI interface.
direction Indicates transmit/receive direction.
turn_request Indicates turn-around request.
turn_disable Indicates turn-around disable.
force_rx_mode Indicates force into receive mode/ wait for stop state.
force_tx_stop_mode Indicates force into transmit mode/ generate stop state.
stop_state Indicates in stop state.
ulps_active_not Indicates ulps state not active.
Error Interface Signals
err_sot_hs Indicates start of transmission (SoT) error.
err_sot_sync_hs Indicates start of transmission synchronization error.
err_esc Indicates escape entry error.
err_sync_esc Indicates low power data transmission synchronization error.
err_control Indicates control error.
err_contention_lp0 Indicates lp0 contention error.
err_contention_lp1 Indicates lp1 contention error.

Debug Interface:

The following signals are available to help debug the CPHY PPI modules

Signal Name Signal Description
Transmitter Side Debug Interface Signals
xmtr_fsm_state Indicates transmitter’s present FSM state.
Receiver Side Debug Interface Signals
rcvr_fsm_state Indicates receiver’s present FSM state.
passive_rcvr_fsm_state Indicates passive receiver’s present FSM state.

 typedef enum  svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::ppi_mode_enum
Type of PPI Mode with Topologies.
PPI_APP_LOCAL( `SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_APP_LOCAL )
Acts as an application layer driving the TX lines and sampling the RX lines.
PPI_PHY_REMOTE( `SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_PHY_REMOTE )
Samples the TX lines and drives the RX lines and also responds to the application DUT like a phy.
PPI_PHY_SERIAL( `SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_PHY_SERIAL )
Samples the TX lines and passes transactions to CPHY serial layer and drives the RX lines based on transactions received through CPHY serial.

TurnRequest de-assertion at PPI I/F happens after one clock of its assertion .
PPI_TURN_REQUEST_UNTIL_BTA( `SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TURN_REQUEST_UNTIL_BTA )
TurnRequest de-assertion at PPI I/F happens after direction flip/Timeout .
PPI_TURN_REQUEST_RANDOM( `SVT_MIPI_CPHY_PPI_TURN_REQUEST_RANDOM )
TurnRequest de-assertion at PPI I/F happens after random delay .

 svt_mipi_cphy_configuration::valid_ranges

Valid range constraint insure that protocol define valid values will be generated for defined configuration variables in process of randomization.
constraint valid_ranges {
    solve calibration_support before calibration_type;
    if ( 1 == 2) {
      ppi_tx_data_width_hs inside {'b01, 'b10};
    }
    else {
      ppi_tx_data_width_hs == 'b01;
    }
    if ( 1 == 2) {
      ppi_rx_data_width_hs inside {'b01, 'b10};
    }
    else {
      ppi_rx_data_width_hs == 'b01;
    }
    ppi_num_of_eot_words_min inside {[ 1 : 10]};
    ppi_num_of_eot_words_max inside {[ 1 : 10]};
    ppi_num_of_eot_words_min >= 1;

     ppi_check_rx_trigger_esc_deassertion_after_rx_clk_esc_cycles_min > 0;
    ppi_check_rx_trigger_esc_deassertion_after_rx_clk_esc_cycles_max >= ppi_check_rx_trigger_esc_deassertion_after_rx_clk_esc_cycles_min;
     (ppi_turn_disable_user_mode == 1'b0) -> (ppi_turn_disable_user_value == 1'b0);

     tgr_preamble_length[6] == 1'b0;
    tgr_post_length <= 5'h1F;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_0_1[2:0] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_0_1[5:3] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_0_1[7:6] == 2'b00;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_2_3[2:0] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_2_3[5:3] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_2_3[7:6] == 2'b00;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_4_5[2:0] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_4_5[5:3] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_4_5[7:6] == 2'b00;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_6_7[2:0] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_6_7[5:3] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_6_7[7:6] == 2'b00;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_8_9[2:0] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_8_9[5:3] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_8_9[7:6] == 2'b00;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_10_11[2:0] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_10_11[5:3] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_10_11[7:6] == 2'b00;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_12_13[2:0] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_12_13[5:3] <= 4;
    tgr_preamble_prog_sequence_12_13[7:6] == 2'b00;
    (preamble_check_en[ 1] == 1) -> tgr_preamble_length[7] == 1'b1;
    solve preamble_check_en before tgr_preamble_length;
         lpdt_byte_pause_duration_min >= 1;
    lpdt_byte_pause_duration_min <= lpdt_byte_pause_duration_max;
    lpdt_byte_pause_duration_max <= 25;
    lpdt_bit_pause_duration_min >= 1;
    lpdt_bit_pause_duration_min <= lpdt_bit_pause_duration_max;
    lpdt_bit_pause_duration_max <= 5;
    num_lpdt_byte_pause_xactions inside {[0 : 5]};
    lpdt_byte_pause_xactions.size() == num_lpdt_byte_pause_xactions;
    num_lpdt_bit_pause inside {[0 : 16]};
    lpdt_bit_pause.size() == num_lpdt_bit_pause;
     lpdt_bit_pause.size() == num_lpdt_bit_pause;
    (lpdt_pause_on_byte_boundary == 1) -> num_lpdt_byte_pause_xactions > 0;
    ((lpdt_pause_on_byte_boundary == 0) && (num_lpdt_bit_pause > 0)) -> num_lpdt_byte_pause_xactions > 0;
     foreach (lpdt_byte_pause_xactions[i]) {
      lpdt_byte_pause_xactions[i] inside {[1 : 100]};
      foreach (lpdt_byte_pause_xactions[j]) {
        if (j < i) {
          lpdt_byte_pause_xactions[j] != lpdt_byte_pause_xactions[i];
        }
      }
    }
     foreach(lpdt_bit_pause[i]) {
      lpdt_bit_pause[i] inside {[0 : ( 16 - 1)]};
      foreach (lpdt_bit_pause[j]) {

          lpdt_bit_pause[j] != lpdt_bit_pause[i];
        }
      }

    trigger_dummy_bytes_min <= trigger_dummy_bytes_max;
    trigger_dummy_bytes_min >= 0;
    trigger_dummy_bytes_max <= 10;
    trigger_dummy_bytes_value inside {[0:2]};
     if(cphy_protocol_version < CPHY_VERSION_12) {
      mode_of_operation == LP_ONLY;
      initialization_type == LP_INITIALIZATION;
    }
    if(mode_of_operation == LP_ONLY) {
      initialization_type == LP_INITIALIZATION;
    }
    if(mode_of_operation == ALP_ONLY) {
      initialization_type == ALP_INITIALIZATION;
    }
    init_alp_pause_wake_wire_state inside {[svt_mipi_cphy_types::PLUS_X:svt_mipi_cphy_types::MINUS_Z]};
    if(cphy_protocol_version >= CPHY_VERSION_12) {
    if(calibration_support == svt_mipi_cphy_types::NO_CALIBRATION_SUPPORT) {
      calibration_type == svt_mipi_cphy_types::NO_CALIBRATION;
    }
    else if(calibration_support == svt_mipi_cphy_types::PREAMBLE_CAL_SUPPORT) {
      calibration_type == svt_mipi_cphy_types::PREAMBLE_CAL;
    }
    else if(calibration_support == svt_mipi_cphy_types::ALT_SEQ_CAL_SUPPORT) {
      calibration_type inside {svt_mipi_cphy_types::PREAMBLE_CAL, svt_mipi_cphy_types::PREAMBLE_ALT_SEQ_CAL};
    }
    else if(calibration_support == svt_mipi_cphy_types::USER_SEQ_CAL_SUPPORT) {
      calibration_type inside {svt_mipi_cphy_types::PREAMBLE_CAL, svt_mipi_cphy_types::PREAMBLE_USER_SEQ_CAL};
    }
    else if(calibration_support == svt_mipi_cphy_types::ALL_CAL_TYPE_SUPPORT) {
      calibration_type inside {svt_mipi_cphy_types::PREAMBLE_CAL, svt_mipi_cphy_types::PREAMBLE_ALT_SEQ_CAL, svt_mipi_cphy_types::PREAMBLE_USER_SEQ_CAL};
    }
    }
    else {
      calibration_support == svt_mipi_cphy_types::NO_CALIBRATION_SUPPORT;
      calibration_type == svt_mipi_cphy_types::NO_CALIBRATION;
    }
